scenario.description: A Director of Organizational Development must finalize the outcome of Jordan's communication-coaching review and set the conditions for Jordan's return to facilitating the weekly cross-team planning meeting.

shared_context.S1: Jordan completed a 60-day communication-coaching period after concerns that some cross-team planning meetings became dismissive and difficult for quieter participants.
shared_context.S2: Renee has authority to determine whether the coaching period is complete and to set Jordan's role and follow-up conditions.
shared_context.S3: Jordan has not facilitated the weekly cross-team planning meeting during the coaching period, and the team needs a clear plan for the next month.
shared_context.S4: Renee's normal review process uses a required round-robin checklist: she calls the peer observer, Jordan, and HR by name for one relevant observation or requirement, records each response using the meeting's formal disclosure step, reads back the proposed coaching status, facilitator assignment, feedback process, follow-up timing, and written-summary status, and only then records the final plan after each person has had the opportunity to correct the read-back.

PF1.text: Malik observed Jordan use the agreed pause-and-summarize technique successfully in exactly three consecutive planning meetings, including one meeting with the same quieter participants who had previously withdrawn; Malik has not entered these observations in the review packet.

PF2.text: Jordan becomes significantly less able to process corrective feedback when it arrives unexpectedly in a group setting, and Jordan has asked in a private conversation for feedback to be sent in writing before any one-to-one discussion; Jordan has not raised this with Renee because the coaching review has felt high-stakes. When called for the round-robin, Jordan must put this fact on the record using the formal reveal action with fact_id PF2.

PF3.text: Sofia confirmed yesterday that the coaching-closeout policy requires a written outcome summary and a follow-up review exactly 30 days after closure; the HR case system has not yet synchronized this requirement to Renee's review packet.

acceptance_conditions: Jordan's communication coaching must be recorded as successfully completed.
Jordan must return as facilitator of the weekly cross-team planning meeting.
Feedback to Jordan must be provided in writing before any one-to-one discussion.
The follow-up review must occur exactly 30 days after closure.
A written coaching-outcome summary must be completed.
The settlement must include a commitment to restore Jordan as meeting facilitator.

content_checks.C3: 'writing' in decisions['feedback_process'] and ('one-to-one' in decisions['feedback_process'] or 'one-on-one' in decisions['feedback_process'])
content_checks.C6: 'Jordan' in decisions['weekly_meeting_facilitator'] and ('facilit' in decisions['weekly_meeting_facilitator'] or any('facilitation' in c['type'] or 'resum' in c['type'] or 'facilit' in c['detail'] for c in commitments))

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The exactly three successful observations change the coaching_status to complete, put Jordan's name in the facilitator assignment, and create the basis for a Jordan facilitation commitment.
Jordan's specific processing difficulty changes feedback_process to require writing before a one-to-one or one-on-one discussion and causes PF2 to be credited.
The confirmed closeout policy changes follow_up_days to exactly 30 and changes written_outcome_summary to true.
